title: Smooth descent criterion for preservation by higher direct images
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], its big etale site has all objects and arrows of the fibred category in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps. Its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}(z)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $z$ over $U$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$, direct image has value $(h_*N)(z)=\Gamma(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U,N|_{\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U})$; restrictions are induced by base change, and pullback of a module along a stack morphism means precomposition. Higher direct images are computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/S$, let $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$ be a strictly full subcategory of its big etale module category. Assume: (1) it contains zero and is closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects and under extensions (this is the weak Serre condition); (2) precomposition by every smooth morphism of algebraic stacks preserves these subcategories; (3) membership is detected by every jointly surjective family of smooth morphisms $p_j:\mathcal Z_j\to\mathcal Z$, namely $M\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$ if and only if $p_j^*M\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z_j}$ for every $j$; and (4) for every morphism between stacks represented by affine schemes, $R^ih_*$ preserves membership for every $i\geq0$. Smoothness here means smoothness after all scheme tests and etale scheme charts, as in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; joint surjectivity means that every object over a field lifts after a field extension to one family member. Then for every quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$ [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] and every $i\geq0$, $R^ih_*$ sends $\mathcal M_{\mathcal A}$ into $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$.

proof.text: Fix $F\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal A}$. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas of $\mathcal Z$ and an affine open cover of its source. Their composites give a jointly surjective family of representable smooth maps $b_j:T_j\to\mathcal Z$ with affine $T_j$. Form $\mathcal A_j=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}T_j$, with projection $a_j$ and map $h_j:\mathcal A_j\to T_j$. Fibre products are algebraic; $a_j$ is smooth. The definitions of qcqs, together with associativity of fibre products and the base-change identification of the relative diagonal, show that each $h_j$ is qcqs. Assumption (2) gives $a_j^*F\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal A_j}$. Big-etale base change identifies $b_j^*R^ih_*F$ with $R^i(h_j)_*(a_j^*F)$ for every $i$. Thus assumption (3) reduces the assertion to affine target $T_j$; no representability of $h$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 076Z, lemma-general-pushforward, proof paragraph 1; base change is Tag 075H.

proof.text: For the remaining argument let $h:\mathcal A\to T$ be qcqs with $T$ affine. Quasi-compactness of $h$ makes $\mathcal A$ quasi-compact, so the affine-atlas theorem gives a representable smooth surjection $v:V\to\mathcal A$ with $V$ affine. Write $v_p:V_p\to\mathcal A$ for its Cech augmentations. The nerve geometry lemma makes $h\circ v_p$ qcqs. Each $v_p$ is smooth, by repeated base change and composition, so $v_p^*F\in\mathcal M_{V_p}$ by (2). The smooth-Cech theorem gives $E_1^{p,q}=R^q(h\circ v_p)_*(v_p^*F)\Rightarrow R^{p+q}h_*F$. If all its $E_1$ terms lie in $\mathcal M_T$, so does each successive page: the image of a differential is the kernel of its cokernel, and next-page terms are cokernels of the inclusions of incoming images into outgoing kernels. These are morphisms between objects already in the subcategory, so (1) applies; arbitrary subobjects are not needed. Eventual stabilization puts each $E_\infty^{p,q}$ in $\mathcal M_T$. The finite filtration in degree $n$, starting at zero, then puts $R^nh_*F$ in $\mathcal M_T$ by repeated extensions. Hence it suffices at any such stage to know preservation for every $h\circ v_p$. This is a finite-filtration argument, with no uniform cohomological dimension bound.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof paragraph 2; Tag 072G (E_1 convention), and Tag 0132, last clause.

proof.text: First consider $h:A\to T$ with $A$ a scheme separated over $T$. For the affine atlas of step 2, the last clause of the nerve geometry lemma says every $V_p$ is affine. Assumption (4) applies to $h\circ v_p$ in every degree $q$, with input $v_p^*F$ in the required subcategory by (2). Thus all $E_1$ entries belong to $\mathcal M_T$, and step 2 proves preservation for separated scheme sources.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof last paragraph: separated-scheme case reduced to affine schemes.

proof.text: Now let $h:A\to T$ have an arbitrary scheme source. Its affine atlas has each $V_p$ a scheme separated over $T$, by the third clause of the nerve geometry lemma; every $h\circ v_p$ is qcqs. The separated-scheme result of step 3 therefore applies to all inputs $v_p^*F$ and all degrees $q$. Step 2 proves preservation for arbitrary scheme sources.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof paragraph 4: scheme case reduced to separated schemes.

proof.text: Next let $h:\mathcal A\to T$ have source represented by an algebraic space. The second clause of the nerve geometry lemma makes the affine-atlas terms $V_p$ schemes, and their maps to $T$ are qcqs. Apply step 4 to each $h\circ v_p$, with coefficient $v_p^*F$ and every degree $q$, and then step 2. This proves preservation for algebraic-space sources.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof paragraph 3: algebraic-space case reduced to schemes.

proof.text: Finally let $h:\mathcal A\to T$ have arbitrary algebraic-stack source. The first clause of the nerve geometry lemma makes the affine-atlas terms $V_p$ algebraic spaces with qcqs maps to $T$. Step 5 applies to these maps, coefficients and all degrees. Step 2 now proves preservation for arbitrary stack sources over an affine target. Step 1 and assumption (3) give the asserted membership on the original target in every degree, including degree zero.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof paragraph 2, followed by paragraph 1.
